_note: Work done in this archive, in the shape Record Atlas imports. See CLAUDE.md. THREE HONESTIES ABOUT THIS FILE. (1) NO ROW CARRIES A WAYPOINT. Every FamilySearch read below was cited by DGS film number and image ark, which is what this archive has always recorded; the atlas keys on the wc=/owc= waypoint and film numbers have matched it zero times. The waypoints could not be recovered on 29 September because the browser pane was recreated and the FamilySearch session was lost - checked in a second tab and read twice before saying so. The film numbers are in a `film` field and no waypoint has been guessed. WHAT COULD BE ATTACHED INSTEAD: every FamilySearch row now carries a `collection` URL, checked against the atlas's own collections.json by the collection TITLE printed on the record page I opened - so these attach as collection marks even though they cannot attach as volume marks. That is a coarser join than a waypoint and it is not a substitute for one. (2) NOTHING BELOW IS `walked`. Every one of these is a plate opened at a known folio, not a register read entry by entry, and saying otherwise would tell the next person a book is finished when it is not. (3) THIS IS A SWEEP, WHICH THE SKILL DISCOURAGES. The instruction to record as-you-go arrived on 29 September, after the work. Rows from earlier sessions are NOT here - see data/sources-consulted.tsv, which lists 24 films, most of them read before this file existed.

src: FamilySearch / City of Cape Town - South Africa, Cape, Cemetery Records 1872-2011; Maitland (Woltemade) Road Cemetery Record of Interments, Volumes 19 and 21
what: LERENA and TAYLOR interments, Cape Town, across three openings in two volumes - image group 102346234 ('Volume 19', 1946-1947) image 208 of 255, and 102346236 ('Volume 21', 1949-1951) image 93 of 252. THREE PLATES AT KNOWN FOLIOS, NOT A WALK: the registers run to tens of thousands of entries and only the pages carrying these surnames were read. NO WAYPOINT WAS ESTABLISHED - this collection is served as numbered IMAGE GROUPS and no wc=/owc= appeared in any URL on the path from the record to the plate, so the image-group numbers are recorded in `film` and nothing has been guessed. THE SURNAME IS WHY THIS NEARLY FAILED: the 1950 burial is indexed as LESINA, and no surname search of any spelling reaches it. It was found by searching GIVEN NAME plus death year within the collection and reading 663 results. That technique is the transferable part. ONE DEFECT WORTH PASSING ON: FamilySearch's own generated citation for image group 102346236 reads 'Maitland, Cape Town, Cape, Cape Colony, Seine-Maritime, France records' - its place matcher resolves this Cape Colony to a French department.

src: FreeREG - Northam (St Margaret) and Bideford, Devon: parish register coverage checked before searching
what: TAYLOR baptisms, Northam and Bideford, 1869-1891, for a daughter born 1882. NOTHING, AND THE NULL IS FULLY EXPLAINED RATHER THAN MERELY RECORDED. FreeREG's own contents pages give Northam, St Margaret, Parish Register: 12,120 records, FIRST 1653, LAST 1817 - the coverage stops sixty-five years before the record wanted. Bideford is listed as a place and has NO church, NO register and NO records at all. So this is a coverage wall, not an absent baptism, and nobody should read the zero as evidence about the family. THE SEARCH WAS RUN ANYWAY, with a control first: surname TAYLOR alone, Northam, 1869-1891, returned 0, which the contents page then explained.

src: findmypast - Devon Baptisms (South West Heritage Trust; transcribed by Devon FHS volunteers); Northam St Margaret, archive reference 1843A/PR/1/16
what: TAYLOR baptisms at Northam, Devon, 1874-1889. SEVEN CHILDREN OF ONE COUPLE RECOVERED IN A SINGLE QUERY, by searching on the MOTHER's forenames rather than each child's - which is the transferable method here, because it is what makes an ABSENCE provable rather than merely unfound. A CONTROL WAS RUN FIRST on the one child whose birth date and address this archive already held, and it returned. ALSO A CONTROLLED NEGATIVE: the candidate tenth child this archive had graded STRONG is not in the series, and the only two same-name baptisms in the county near the date belong to two other men of the same name, identified by their wives' forenames. The candidate was downgraded on the strength of it.

src: General Register Office (gro.gov.uk) - the GRO's own online birth index for England and Wales
what: TAYLOR births with mother's maiden surname BRAYLEY, Bideford district, 1870-1893. TEN SEARCHES - five year-windows times two sexes, because sex is a mandatory field and the year range is capped at plus or minus two. NINE CHILDREN OF ONE COUPLE RECOVERED, AND A TENTH DISPROVED. THE POINT OF THIS SOURCE, which no free index can match: the GRO's own index PRINTS THE MOTHER'S MAIDEN SURNAME on every birth from 1837, so a search on father's surname plus mother's maiden name returns a couple's children BY DEFINITION rather than by inference. FreeBMD carries no mother's maiden name in its birth index and never will, which is why three weeks of candidate-weighing there could not settle what this settled in ten searches. THE CRITICAL WINDOW WAS RE-RUN ON 'SIMILAR SOUNDING VARIATIONS' because a spelling variant of the mother's surname was documented in an earlier census: 28 births across England, the same two in the district. IT NEEDS AN ACCOUNT, which the archive owner signed in; this session does not create accounts.
